items.title: Place cells: How your brain creates maps of abstract spaces
items.description:
=====
My name is Artem, I'm a neuroscience PhD student at Harvard University. 
🌎 Website and Social links: https://kirsanov.ai/
📥 "Receptive Field" neuro-newsletter: https://artemkirsanov.substack.com/
✨ Support me on Patreon to get access to Discord community: https://patreon.com/artemkirsanov
=====

In this video, we will explore the positional system of the brain - hippocampal place cells. We will see how it relates to contextual memory and mapping of more abstract features.

🕒 OUTLINE:
00:00
items.why_watch: Artem Kirsanov, a Harvard neuroscience PhD student, explains hippocampal place cells — the neurons that fire in specific locations to build your brain's internal map — and then makes the bigger, stranger claim: the same system may be how your brain maps abstract conceptual spaces, not just physical ones. The animation is genuinely clarifying rather than decorative, and the final implications for how we organize memory and thought are worth sitting with. One of the more rewarding 15-minute science videos around.

items.why_watch: Professor Milton Mermikides covers genuinely surprising ground here — from how Debussy engineered dreamlike sound through specific harmonic choices, to the neurological question of whether music continues to 'exist' for us during sleep. The section on lullabies as cultural artifacts and the tantalizing question of recovering music heard in dreams make this more than a standard musicology lecture. Nearly 50 minutes, but the chapter markers let you graze by topic.

items.title: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire by Edward Gibbon Volume I Chapter XII
items.description:
The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire is a six-volume work by the English historian Edward Gibbon. The work traces Western civilization along with the Islamic and Mongolian conquests, from the height of the Roman Empire to the fall of Byzantium in the fifteenth century. 

Gibbon's mammoth work is among the most magnificent and ambitious narratives in European literature. Its subject is the fate of one of the world's greatest civilizations over thirteen centuries - its rulers, w
items.why_watch: This is an audiobook reading of Chapter XII of Gibbon's 'Decline and Fall' — not analysis, just the original text delivered cleanly for listening. At 72 minutes it's a commitment, but if you've been meaning to actually read Gibbon rather than read about him, this is a low-friction way to let one of history's great prose stylists wash over you on a walk or commute. Best approached as an audio experience rather than a video.

items.title: GOOD NEWS: Skin Cancer Vaccine, NY Moratorium on Data Centers, Sweden Abandons Technology in Schools
items.description:
In today’s video, we’re taking a break from all the doom and gloom to talk about positive developments happening around the world.

From promising advances in cancer treatment and mRNA vaccine research to changes happening in Sweden’s classrooms, there are some fascinating stories worth celebrating and discussing. 

Sometimes the internet can make it feel like everything is going wrong, but good things are happening too and we’re going to shine a light on them!
items.why_watch: A deliberately low-key good-news roundup covering a skin cancer mRNA vaccine update, New York's data center moratorium, and Sweden quietly reversing its all-technology classroom experiment — three stories that each push back against a dominant narrative in a different way. The channel is tiny and the production is simple, but the curation is thoughtful and the stories are real. A reasonable antidote to doom-scrolling, without any of the forced optimism.

discovery_articles.title: Jingling Pot in England
discovery_articles.snippet: Jingling Pot is one of the most popular vertical cave systems in the West Kingsdale area of Yorkshire. The cave, or as is known locally, pothole (pit cave in American English), is on the flanks of one of Yorkshires finest mountains, Wherneside. It is about 145 feet deep and explorers have the option of a direct abseil (rappel) descent down the main shaft or, a  traverse, a few feet from the top into the Lateral Cleft.

discovery_articles.title: Bunski Kanal in Malo Polje, Bosnia and Herzegovina
discovery_articles.snippet: Tucked away just a few minutes from Mostar, Bunski Kanal is one of Bosnia and Herzegovina's most overlooked natural treasures. Here, the emerald-green Buna River squeezes through a narrow limestone channel before merging with the larger Neretva River, creating a striking display of swirling currents, vivid colors, and raw natural power. Despite its proximity to popular attractions like Mostar and Blagaj, surprisingly few travelers stop here.

news.title: Cocktail of the week: Cafe Cùil’s Buckfast bloody Maìri – recipe | The good mixer
news.snippet: The favourite spicy brunch cocktail gets a Scottish twist, complete with Buckfast and a slice of pickle for punch This is our take on the ultimate brunch cocktail, though of course we had to give it a Gaelic stamp of some kind, so have added a shot of Buckfast and renamed it Maìri. If you’re not familiar, Buckfast is a sweet tonic wine, apparently known for its “healing” properties, made in Devon by Benedictine monks, but that has been adopted by the Scots as our own. Clare Coghill, chef-owner, Café Cùil , Isle of Skye Continue reading...
news.blurb: A Bloody Mary with a distinctly Scottish soul, this Buckfast-laced brunch cocktail is the kind of gloriously unhinged twist that makes you genuinely glad someone thought of it.
